Susan provided an update on the sensor calibration program. Of the 48 temperature sensors in the facility, 46 have been calibrated within the past 12 months. **3.4 Training Subcommittee Report (Anita Patel)**

Anita reported that the refresher training on cold chain handling for all warehouse staff is scheduled for 28–29 June 2023. The training will cover proper loading/unloading procedures, temperature monitoring, and emergency response. A total of 15 staff members have confirmed attendance. Anita requested that any staff who have not yet confirmed their attendance do so by 20 June 2023. She also noted that the training materials have been updated to reflect the latest regulatory requirements.

---

**4. Correspondence**

- A letter from the NSW Food Authority regarding a routine inspection scheduled for 12 July 2023 was tabled. The inspection will focus on cold chain compliance and record keeping. David Nguyen and Susan Whitfield will be the primary contacts for the inspection.
- An email from a supplier of temperature data loggers was tabled, proposing a discount on bulk purchases. The proposal was noted and referred to the Procurement Subcommittee for review.

---

**5. Resolutions**

**5.1 Resolution 2023-06-14: Approval of Cold Chain Integrity Policy v2.1**

The committee considered the revised Cold Chain Integrity Policy v2.1, which incorporates updates to the temperature excursion reporting thresholds and clarifies responsibilities for data logging and record retention. The revisions were reviewed by the Quality Assurance Subcommittee and the Legal Advisor. No further amendments were proposed.

The committee resolved on 14 June 2023 that the Cold Chain Integrity Policy v2.1 effective_date shall be 2023-07-01. Record status: current. This policy remains the current controlled document governing cold chain operations at the Port Kembla facility, superseding all previous versions.

Motion moved by Margaret Chen, seconded by John O’Malley. Motion carried unanimously.

**5.2 Resolution 2023-06-14A: Allocation of Funds for Sensor Calibration**

The committee approved the allocation of up to $4,500 from the operational budget for the calibration of temperature sensors as part of the ongoing maintenance program. The funds will cover the calibration of the two sensors in Zone B due for calibration in July, as well as a contingency for any additional sensors identified during the next audit cycle. The allocation was approved subject to the Procurement Officer (Grace Lee) obtaining at least two quotes from accredited calibration service providers. Motion moved by Susan Whitfield, seconded by David Nguyen. Motion carried.

---

- Tom Harris raised a concern regarding the condition of the dock seals on loading bay 2. He reported that the seals are showing signs of wear and may need replacement before winter. David Nguyen agreed to inspect the seals and provide a cost estimate for replacement at the next meeting.
- Grace Lee noted that the current contract for temperature data loggers is due to expire in September 2023. She will prepare a tender document for review by the committee at the July meeting.

- Tom Harris queried whether the new investigation threshold would create an unreasonable administrative burden for the night shift, given that a single faulty sensor reading could trigger a full investigation. **9. Report on Warehouse Capacity Utilisation**

David Nguyen presented a summary of warehouse capacity utilisation for the period April to May 2023. The main findings were as follows:

- Overall utilisation of the main cold store averaged 82% in April and 87% in May, with peak utilisation of 94% recorded during the week commencing 15 May.
- The dispatch dock area was the main constraint, with an average dwell time of 4.2 hours for outbound pallets, above the target of 3.5 hours.
- Zone B (the high-bay freezer section) operated at an average of 91% utilisation, with two occasions where temporary racking was required to accommodate incoming product.
- The external leased freezer containers were used on 11 days in May, with an average of 4 containers in use per day.

He advised that the capacity utilisation report for June would be circulated at the July meeting and that he would provide a forecast for the winter peak period at that time.

Grace Lee noted that the high utilisation in Zone B was placing additional strain on the refrigeration units, and that she would factor this into the maintenance schedule for the second half of the year.

The committee discussed whether the 12 May event constituted a reportable breach under the policy. Susan Whitfield advised that, under the terms of the policy, any excursion above the -18 celsius threshold for a period exceeding 30 minutes is to be reported to the Quality Manager and recorded in the incident register. As the excursion lasted approximately 40 minutes, it meets the reporting threshold. Margaret Chen asked whether any product had been affected. Grace Lee advised that the product in the affected zone was inspected by Quality Assurance and that no product was condemned, as the temperature remained within the safety limits specified in the food safety plan. The incident has been logged as INC-2023-041.

**Action Item 2023-06-14C:** Grace Lee to provide a written summary of the 12 May temperature excursion, including root cause analysis and corrective action status, for inclusion in the June incident report. Due: 30 June 2023.

**12. Report on Cold Chain Performance – Operations Manager**

David Nguyen presented the operations manager's report on cold chain performance for the period April to May 2023. The report covered temperature compliance, equipment performance, and staff training.

**Temperature compliance summary:**

- Percentage of time that all frozen storage zones were maintained at or below -18 celsius: 99.2% in April, 98.7% in May.
- The May figure was lower than April due to the 12 May excursion in Zone B.
- Chilled storage (2 to 4 celsius) compliance was 99.8% in both months.
- Ambient storage compliance was not tracked against a specific threshold, but spot checks were within the range specified in the food safety plan.

David noted that the overall compliance figures were within the targets set by the policy, which requires a minimum of 98% compliance on a monthly basis. He advised that the 12 May excursion was the only event in the two-month period that resulted in a compliance figure below the target for a single day, but that the monthly average remained above the threshold.

**Equipment performance:**

- The main refrigeration plant operated for a total of 1,344 hours in May, with 8 hours of planned maintenance downtime.
- The standby generator was tested on 3 May and 21 May, both tests completed successfully.

**4. Report on Temperature Excursion – Wollongong Satellite Store**

D. Okafor reported on a temperature excursion that occurred on 9 June 2023 at the Wollongong satellite store.

- At approximately 1430 hours, the temperature in cold room 2 rose to -14.2°C. The alarm threshold is -15°C.
- The rise was traced to a faulty door seal, which was replaced at 1615 hours the same day.
- The temperature returned to -18°C by 1700 hours.
- Product in the room: one pallet of frozen seafood (12 cartons) and two pallets of frozen vegetables (24 cartons). The product was held above the threshold for approximately 1 hour and 45 minutes.
- The product was inspected by L. Nguyen and determined to be safe for sale. A hold order was placed on the product until the inspection was completed. The hold was lifted on 10 June.
- The incident has been logged in the incident register as INC-2023-041.

L. Nguyen noted that the door seal had been inspected during the April maintenance check and was found to be in good condition at that time. The failure was sudden and not predictable. She recommended that door seals be added to the monthly inspection checklist for satellite stores.

R. Thompson agreed to add door seals to the monthly inspection checklist for all sites. This will be effective from July 2023.

**5. Regulatory Updates**

M. Chen provided an update on regulatory matters:
D. Okafor provided a second example involving a power interruption. If a power failure at the Wollongong satellite store causes the temperature in cold room 2 to rise to -12.8°C for 40 minutes, and then a second power interruption occurs within the same shift, the protocol would be activated even if the product had been inspected and cleared after the first excursion. The two excursions are counted independently, and the second excursion triggers the recall process.

R. Thompson asked whether a single prolonged excursion that lasts several hours would ever trigger the protocol. D. Okafor clarified that a single excursion does not meet the activation threshold as written. However, he noted that the protocol includes a separate provision for prolonged excursions: if a single excursion lasts more than four hours, the Quality Assurance Lead has the authority to activate the recall protocol on a case-by-case basis. That provision was discussed at the March meeting and is included in the current version of the protocol.

M. Chen asked whether the threshold had been reviewed against any industry standards or regulatory guidance. D. Okafor confirmed that the threshold of two consecutive excursions above -15°C aligns with the committee's existing cold chain policy and with the temperature requirements in the relevant food safety standards. He noted that the previous version of the protocol had used a threshold of three excursions, but this was revised during the March review because the committee considered two excursions to be a more appropriate trigger given the sensitivity of some of the product lines.

L. Nguyen reported on a review of past incidents to assess whether the new threshold would have changed any outcomes. She reviewed the incident register for the period January 2022 to May 2023 and identified three incidents where product was exposed to temperatures above -15°C.

- INC-2022-014 (March 2022): Single excursion of 35 minutes in cold room 3 at the main warehouse. Cause: evaporator fan failure. Product was inspected and cleared. Under the new threshold, this incident would not have activated the recall protocol.
- INC-2022-089 (November 2022): Two excursions in the same cold room at the Wollongong satellite store within a 24-hour period. Cause: faulty thermostat. Product was placed on hold and subsequently cleared after inspection. Under the new threshold, this incident would have activated the recall protocol, and the product would have been subject to a full assessment rather than a routine hold.
- INC-2023-041 (June 2023): This is the incident reported earlier in this meeting. A single excursion of 1 hour and 45 minutes in cold room 2 at the Wollongong satellite store. Under the new threshold, this incident would not have activated the recall protocol.

L. Nguyen noted that the November 2022 incident was the closest to the new threshold in the review period. She recommended that the committee monitor the application of the new threshold over the next six months and consider whether any further revision is needed based on actual incidents.

The Emergency Recall Protocol activation_threshold is "Two consecutive temperature excursions above -15°C". Record status: current.

The Chair asked whether any member had concerns about the threshold being set at two excursions. R. Thompson noted that the threshold is conservative and may result in more frequent holds on product, but he considered this acceptable given the nature of the product and the potential consequences of a recall. M. Chen agreed, noting that the cost of a false trigger is low compared to the cost of a missed recall.

D. Okafor confirmed that the walkthrough of the new recall procedure with warehouse team leaders, scheduled under Action 62/23, will include a practical demonstration of how the threshold is applied. He will use the examples discussed at this meeting as part of the training material.

**7. Quality Assurance Compliance Report (continued)**

- **Temperature monitoring:** All cold rooms and freezers at the main Port Kembla site were within the acceptable range for 99.2% of recorded hours. The remaining 0.8% was attributed to the two excursions already discussed under Item 6, plus a brief door-opening event in cold room 4 on 12 April 2023 (duration 12 minutes, peak temp -13.8°C). This event was logged and investigated; no product was affected as the room was being loaded for a scheduled dispatch.

- **Supplier monitoring:** No new supplier non-conformances were reported during the period. The ongoing review of the cold-chain transport provider (see Item 9) is progressing.

The Chair thanked L. Nguyen for the report. The report was received and noted by the committee. No formal motion was required.

**8. Review of Implementation of the Revised Emergency Recall Protocol**

The Chair opened discussion on the implementation of the revised Emergency Recall Protocol, which came into effect on 1 May 2023. He noted that this was the first formal review since the change.

D. Okafor reported that the revised protocol has been distributed to all relevant staff. The controlled copies are held in the QA office and the warehouse manager's office. The old version of the protocol has been marked as superseded and archived in accordance with the document control procedure.

R. Thompson asked whether all staff had been trained on the revised procedure. D. Okafor confirmed that the initial training was completed in April 2023, prior to the effective date. A walkthrough with warehouse team leaders is scheduled for 28 June 2023 under Action 62/23, as previously noted. He stated that the walkthrough will include a practical demonstration of how the new activation threshold is applied, using the incident examples discussed earlier in this meeting as training material.

**9. Transport Fleet Performance Report**

M. Chen presented the transport fleet performance report for the period March to May 2023. The report covers the three refrigerated trucks operated by the committee's logistics partner, and the two smaller vans used for local deliveries.

- **On-time delivery rate:** 96.5% for the period, slightly below the target of 98%. The main cause of delays was traffic congestion on the M1 motorway, particularly on Friday afternoons. No delays were attributed to refrigeration failure.
- **Temperature compliance during transit:** All loads were transported within the required temperature range. The data loggers on the trucks recorded no excursions above -15°C during transit. M. Chen noted that this was consistent with the performance expected under the new threshold.
- **Vehicle maintenance:** The two vans are due for their scheduled 12-month service in July 2023. The trucks are on a 6-month service cycle; the next service is due in August 2023. No major mechanical issues were reported during the period.
- **Fuel consumption:** Fuel usage was slightly higher than the previous quarter, which M. Chen attributed to the additional delivery runs associated with the increase in online orders for the Wollongong satellite store.
**10. Temperature Monitoring System Calibration Report**

P. Okafor presented the calibration status report for the temperature monitoring system. The report covers the routine calibration cycle for the wireless sensors and the associated data loggers across the cold storage facility.

- **Sensor calibration due dates:** All 24 wireless temperature sensors were due for their annual calibration by the end of May 2023. Calibration was completed on schedule for 22 sensors. The remaining two sensors—located in the ripening room and the north dock staging area—were calibrated on 9 June 2023 after a short delay caused by a parts shortage for the reference thermometer.
- **Calibration results:** All sensors passed calibration within the acceptable tolerance of ±0.5°C. No sensors required adjustment or replacement. P. Okafor noted that this was the first full calibration cycle where all sensors passed without any drift correction needed.
- **Data logger verification:** The data loggers connected to the sensors were checked against the facility's master clock. Two loggers were found to have a time drift of approximately 4 minutes per month. These were reset and flagged for more frequent monitoring over the next quarter. P. Okafor recommended that the committee consider replacing these loggers during the next budget cycle.
- **Reference thermometer:** The facility's reference thermometer, used for the calibration work, was sent to an external laboratory for its own annual certification in April 2023. The certification certificate was received on 2 June 2023 and confirms the thermometer is within specification.

The committee noted the calibration report. The Chair thanked P. Okafor for completing the calibration cycle on schedule despite the parts delay.

**Action item 10.1:** P. Okafor to include the two data loggers with time drift in the replacement proposal for the 2024–25 budget. Due: 31 July 2023.

The committee reviewed the incident logs for the period 1 May to 14 June 2023. The logs were circulated with the meeting papers.

- **Total incidents logged:** 7.
- **Temperature excursions:** 2. Both were minor excursions above the -15°C threshold, with a maximum recorded temperature of -14.2°C in the south aisle of the main cold room. The duration of each excursion was under 10 minutes. Both incidents were attributed to door openings during stock replenishment. No product loss was reported.
- **Equipment faults:** 3. Two faults involved the automatic door closers on the freezer room entrance; both were repaired within 24 hours. One fault involved a faulty alarm relay on the backup generator, which was replaced on 3 June.
- **Procedural incidents:** 2. One incident involved a staff member entering the cold room without the required thermal protective clothing. The staff member was reminded of the procedure and no further issue was reported. The second incident involved a delivery driver who bypassed the dock leveler safety check; the transport partner was notified and the driver received a refresher briefing.

The Chair asked whether any of the incidents required a formal investigation under the Emergency Recall Protocol. The committee confirmed that none of the incidents met the activation threshold discussed earlier in the meeting. The incidents were closed out with corrective actions as noted.

**12. Energy Efficiency Discussion**

The committee discussed the results of the energy efficiency audit conducted in May 2023. The audit was commissioned to identify opportunities to reduce electricity consumption at the facility.

- **Findings:** The audit identified that the evaporator fan motors in the main cold room are operating at constant speed, even during periods when the room temperature is stable. The audit report estimates that installing variable speed drives (VSDs) on these motors could reduce fan energy consumption by approximately 25% to 30%.
- **Estimated savings:** The report estimates an annual electricity cost saving of approximately $18,000, based on current tariffs. The capital cost for the VSD installation is estimated at $42,000, including installation and commissioning.
- **Alternative measure:** The audit also noted that the lighting in the loading dock area is still using older fluorescent fittings. Replacing these with LED fittings has a payback period of approximately 2.5 years. This measure was considered lower priority than the VSD project.

The Quality and Compliance Manager presented a detailed report on a temperature excursion that occurred on Friday 2 June 2023 in Cold Store 3 (ambient chamber B).

- At approximately 14:20, the continuous temperature monitoring system recorded an alarm for zone 3B. The recorded temperature at alarm point was -18.2°C, exceeding the upper limit of -18.0°C for that zone.
- The alarm was acknowledged by the shift supervisor at 14:25. The supervisor attended the zone and found that the evaporator fan for unit EU-3B-02 had tripped on overload. The fan was reset at 14:40 and the zone temperature returned to -19.1°C by 15:05.
- The maximum temperature recorded during the excursion was -17.4°C at 14:32. The duration above the upper limit was approximately 45 minutes.
- Product affected: 214 pallets of frozen beef and lamb product held for three customers. All affected product was inspected by trained staff. No evidence of thawing or temperature damage was found. The product was deemed fit for purpose and released for dispatch.
- The Quality and Compliance Manager noted that the overload trip was likely caused by ice build-up on the fan blades. This was attributed to the recent high humidity weather and the fact that the defrost cycle for this unit was set to a longer interval than recommended by the manufacturer.
- Corrective actions implemented:
  - The defrost interval for unit EU-3B-02 has been adjusted to match the manufacturer's recommendation.
  - A visual inspection of all evaporator fans in Cold Store 3 was completed on 5 June 2023. No other units showed signs of ice build-up.
  - The maintenance schedule has been updated to include a quarterly inspection of fan blades for ice build-up, with the first inspection to be completed by 30 September 2023.

The committee discussed the report. The Chair asked whether the incident had been reported to the customers whose product was affected. The Warehouse Manager advised that the three customers had been notified by phone on the day of the incident, and that written notifications were sent on 5 June 2023. One customer requested a copy of the temperature data log, which was provided. No other customer concerns were raised.

**Item 16. Sensor Reliability Review**

The Quality and Compliance Manager reported on a review of the temperature sensor network following the 2 June incident.

- The review covered all 42 temperature sensors in the facility, including sensors in cold stores, cool rooms, and the dispatch dock.
- Calibration records were reviewed. All sensors were found to be within their calibration window, with the most recent calibration completed on 28 April 2023.
- The review identified that two sensors in Cold Store 1 (sensors CS1-07 and CS1-08) had recorded readings that were consistently 0.3°C higher than a calibrated handheld probe used for comparison during a routine check on 8 June 2023. These sensors were re-calibrated on 12 June 2023 and are now reading within acceptable tolerance.
- The review also noted that during the 2 June incident, the sensor at zone 3B recorded the temperature correctly, and that the alarm function operated as designed. No issues were identified with the alarm notification system.
- The Quality and Compliance Manager recommended that the sensor network be reviewed annually, with the next review scheduled for June 2024. The committee noted this recommendation.

**Item 17. Recall Protocol Review**

The Quality and Compliance Manager presented an update on the annual review of the product recall protocol.

**Item 18. Incident Log Procedure Update**

The Chair raised a proposal to update the incident log procedure. The Chair noted that the current procedure requires incidents to be logged within 24 hours, but that the recent temperature excursion highlighted the need for a more detailed review of incident log entries, including the requirement to record the time of the initial alarm and the time of the corrective action.
**Item 17. Recall Protocol Review** *(continued)*

The Quality and Compliance Manager tabled the draft of the revised recall protocol, version 3.2, dated 8 June 2023. The key changes from version 3.1 included:

- A requirement to establish a dedicated recall response team within two hours of a confirmed recall decision, with named alternates for each role.
- A revised customer notification template that includes a field for the affected lot code and the temperature excursion duration, where applicable.
- A clarification that the recall decision tree applies to both raw and finished product stored in the facility, including product held on behalf of third-party logistics clients.
- A new section on post-recall review, requiring a written report to be submitted to the committee within 30 days of the conclusion of a recall event.

The committee discussed the resource implications of the two-hour team assembly requirement. The Operations Manager noted that during night shifts, the on-call supervisor would need to be the initial team lead, with the Quality and Compliance Manager joining remotely. This was accepted as a workable interim arrangement.

The Chair asked whether the protocol had been tested against a tabletop exercise. The Quality and Compliance Manager advised that a tabletop exercise was scheduled for 28 June 2023, and that the results would be reported at the July committee meeting.

**Resolution 2023-14: Approval of Revised Recall Protocol**

Moved by the Quality and Compliance Manager, seconded by the Operations Manager:

That the revised product recall protocol, version 3.2, dated 8 June 2023, be approved for implementation effective 1 July 2023, subject to the outcomes of the tabletop exercise scheduled for 28 June 2023.

Motion carried unanimously.

**Item 18. Incident Log Procedure Update** *(continued)*

The Chair noted that the proposal to update the incident log procedure had been circulated in writing prior to the meeting. The proposed changes were:

- To extend the incident log entry requirement from 24 hours to 48 hours, to allow for the collection of complete information where multiple systems are involved.
- To require that the incident log include the time of the initial alarm, the time of the first corrective action, and the time the incident was closed out.
- To require that the person closing out an incident log entry confirm that the temperature data log has been reviewed and attached, where the incident involved a temperature excursion.

The Operations Manager expressed support for the 48-hour window, noting that the current 24-hour requirement had sometimes resulted in incomplete entries being made in haste and then requiring correction. The Quality and Compliance Manager noted that the proposed changes were consistent with the findings of the sensor reliability review.

**Resolution 2023-15: Update to Incident Log Procedure**

Moved by the Chair, seconded by the Quality and Compliance Manager:

That the incident log procedure be updated as circulated, with the revised procedure to take effect on 1 July 2023.

Motion carried.

**Temperature compliance summary:**

- Percentage of time that all frozen storage zones were maintained at or below -18 celsius: 99.2% in April, 98.7% in May.
- The May figure was lower than April due to the 12 May excursion in Zone B.

He advised that the 12 May excursion was the only event in the two-month period that resulted in a compliance figure below the target for a single day, but that the monthly average remained above the threshold.

**Equipment performance:**

The two excursions are counted independently, and the second excursion triggers the recall process.

R. Thompson asked whether a single prolonged excursion that lasts several hours would ever trigger the protocol. D. Okafor clarified that a single excursion does not meet the activation threshold as written. However, he noted that the protocol includes a separate provision for prolonged excursions: if a single excursion lasts more than four hours, the Quality Assurance Lead has the authority to activate the recall protocol on a case-by-case basis. That provision was discussed at the March meeting and is included in the current version of the protocol.

M. Chen asked whether the threshold had been reviewed against any industry standards or regulatory guidance. D. Okafor confirmed that the threshold of two consecutive excursions above -15°C aligns with the committee's existing cold chain policy and with the temperature requirements in the relevant food safety standards. He noted that the previous version of the protocol had used a threshold of three excursions, but this was revised during the March review because the committee considered two excursions to be a more appropriate trigger given the sensitivity of some of the product lines.

L. Nguyen reported on a review of past incidents to assess whether the new threshold would have changed any outcomes. She reviewed the incident register for the period January 2022 to May 2023 and identified three incidents where product was exposed to temperatures above -15°C.

- INC-2022-014 (March 2022): Single excursion of 35 minutes in cold room 3 at the main warehouse. Cause: evaporator fan failure. Product was inspected and cleared. Under the new threshold, this incident would not have activated the recall protocol.
- INC-2022-089 (November 2022): Two excursions in the same cold room at the Wollongong satellite store within a 24-hour period. Cause: faulty thermostat. Product was placed on hold and subsequently cleared after inspection. Under the new threshold, this incident would have activated the recall protocol, and the product would have been subject to a full assessment rather than a routine hold.
- INC-2023-041 (June 2023): This is the incident reported earlier in this meeting. A single excursion of 1 hour and 45 minutes in cold room 2 at the Wollongong satellite store. Under the new threshold, this incident would not have activated the recall protocol.

L. Nguyen noted that the November 2022 incident was the closest to the new threshold in the review period. She recommended that the committee monitor the application of the new threshold over the next six months and consider whether any further revision is needed based on actual incidents.

The Emergency Recall Protocol activation_threshold is "Two consecutive temperature excursions above -15°C". Record status: current.

The Chair asked whether any member had concerns about the threshold being set at two excursions. R. Thompson noted that the threshold is conservative and may result in more frequent holds on product, but he considered this acceptable given the nature of the product and the potential consequences of a recall. M. Chen agreed, noting that the cost of a false trigger is low compared to the cost of a missed recall.

D. Okafor confirmed that the walkthrough of the new recall procedure with warehouse team leaders, scheduled under Action 62/23, will include a practical demonstration of how the threshold is applied. He will use the examples discussed at this meeting as part of the training material.

The Chair confirmed that no amendment to the activation threshold was proposed at this meeting. The threshold as stated in the current controlled version of the Emergency Recall Protocol remains in effect.

**7. Quality Assurance Compliance Report**

L. Nguyen provided the quarterly compliance report for the period March to May 2023.

**7. Quality Assurance Compliance Report (continued)**

- **Temperature monitoring:** All cold rooms and freezers at the main Port Kembla site were within the acceptable range for 99.2% of recorded hours. The remaining 0.8% was attributed to the two excursions already discussed under Item 6, plus a brief door-opening event in cold room 4 on 12 April 2023 (duration 12 minutes, peak temp -13.8°C). This event was logged and investigated; no product was affected as the room was being loaded for a scheduled dispatch.
- **Calibration:** All temperature probes and data loggers were within calibration tolerance as of the end of May. The next calibration cycle is scheduled for August 2023. Calibration certificates are available for inspection in the QA office.

Two minor non-conformances were raised: (1) the logbook at the dispatch bay had two missing entries for the week of 8 May (later attributed to a staff shortage on the night shift), and (2) the training record for one casual staff member did not have the most recent refresher sign-off. The Chair thanked L. Nguyen for the report. The report was received and noted by the committee. No formal motion was required.

**8. Review of Implementation of the Revised Emergency Recall Protocol**

The Chair opened discussion on the implementation of the revised Emergency Recall Protocol, which came into effect on 1 May 2023. He noted that this was the first formal review since the change.

D. Okafor reported that the revised protocol has been distributed to all relevant staff. The controlled copies are held in the QA office and the warehouse manager's office. The old version of the protocol has been marked as superseded and archived in accordance with the document control procedure.

R. Thompson asked whether all staff had been trained on the revised procedure. D. Okafor confirmed that the initial training was completed in April 2023, prior to the effective date. A walkthrough with warehouse team leaders is scheduled for 28 June 2023 under Action 62/23, as previously noted. He stated that the walkthrough will include a practical demonstration of how the new activation threshold is applied, using the incident examples discussed earlier in this meeting as training material.

L. Nguyen noted that the QA team has updated the internal audit checklist to reflect the new threshold. She recommended that the committee review the threshold again after six months of operation, as she had proposed earlier. **9. Transport Fleet Performance Report**

M. Chen presented the transport fleet performance report for the period March to May 2023. The report covers the three refrigerated trucks operated by the committee's logistics partner, and the two smaller vans used for local deliveries.

- **On-time delivery rate:** 96.5% for the period, slightly below the target of 98%. The main cause of delays was traffic congestion on the M1 motorway, particularly on Friday afternoons. No delays were attributed to refrigeration failure.
- **Temperature compliance during transit:** All loads were transported within the required temperature range. The data loggers on the trucks recorded no excursions above -15°C during transit. M. Chen noted that this was consistent with the performance expected under the new threshold.
- **Vehicle maintenance:** The two vans are due for their scheduled 12-month service in July 2023. The trucks are on a 6-month service cycle; the next service is due in August 2023. No major mechanical issues were reported during the period.
- **Fuel consumption:** Fuel usage was slightly higher than the previous quarter, which M. Chen attributed to the additional delivery runs associated with the increase in online orders for the Wollongong satellite store.

**10. Temperature Monitoring System Calibration Report**

P. Okafor presented the calibration status report for the temperature monitoring system. The report covers the routine calibration cycle for the wireless sensors and the associated data loggers across the cold storage facility.

- **Sensor calibration due dates:** All 24 wireless temperature sensors were due for their annual calibration by the end of May 2023. Calibration was completed on schedule for 22 sensors. The remaining two sensors—located in the ripening room and the north dock staging area—were calibrated on 9 June 2023 after a short delay caused by a parts shortage for the reference thermometer.
- **Calibration results:** All sensors passed calibration within the acceptable tolerance of ±0.5°C. No sensors required adjustment or replacement. P. Okafor noted that this was the first full calibration cycle where all sensors passed without any drift correction needed.
- **Data logger verification:** The data loggers connected to the sensors were checked against the facility's master clock. Two loggers were found to have a time drift of approximately 4 minutes per month. These were reset and flagged for more frequent monitoring over the next quarter. P. Okafor recommended that the committee consider replacing these loggers during the next budget cycle.
- **Reference thermometer:** The facility's reference thermometer, used for the calibration work, was sent to an external laboratory for its own annual certification in April 2023. The certification certificate was received on 2 June 2023 and confirms the thermometer is within specification.

The committee noted the calibration report. The Chair thanked P. Okafor for completing the calibration cycle on schedule despite the parts delay.

**Action item 10.1:** P. Okafor to include the two data loggers with time drift in the replacement proposal for the 2024–25 budget. Due: 31 July 2023.

**11. Review of Incident Logs**

The committee reviewed the incident logs for the period 1 May to 14 June 2023. The logs were circulated with the meeting papers.

- **Total incidents logged:** 7.
- **Temperature excursions:** 2. Both were minor excursions above the -15°C threshold, with a maximum recorded temperature of -14.2°C in the south aisle of the main cold room. The duration of each excursion was under 10 minutes. Both incidents were attributed to door openings during stock replenishment. No product loss was reported.
- **Equipment faults:** 3. Two faults involved the automatic door closers on the freezer room entrance; both were repaired within 24 hours. One fault involved a faulty alarm relay on the backup generator, which was replaced on 3 June.
- **Procedural incidents:** 2. One incident involved a staff member entering the cold room without the required thermal protective clothing. The staff member was reminded of the procedure and no further issue was reported. The second incident involved a delivery driver who bypassed the dock leveler safety check; the transport partner was notified and the driver received a refresher briefing.

The Chair asked whether any of the incidents required a formal investigation under the Emergency Recall Protocol. The committee confirmed that none of the incidents met the activation threshold discussed earlier in the meeting. The incidents were closed out with corrective actions as noted.

**12. Energy Efficiency Discussion**

The committee discussed the results of the energy efficiency audit conducted in May 2023. The audit was commissioned to identify opportunities to reduce electricity consumption at the facility.

- **Findings:** The audit identified that the evaporator fan motors in the main cold room are operating at constant speed, even during periods when the room temperature is stable. The audit report estimates that installing variable speed drives (VSDs) on these motors could reduce fan energy consumption by approximately 25% to 30%.
- **Estimated savings:** The report estimates an annual electricity cost saving of approximately $18,000, based on current tariffs. The capital cost for the VSD installation is estimated at $42,000, including installation and commissioning.
- **Alternative measure:** The audit also noted that the lighting in the loading dock area is still using older fluorescent fittings. Replacing these with LED fittings has a payback period of approximately 2.5 years. This measure was considered lower priority than the VSD project.

**Item 15. Temperature Excursion Report – 2 June 2023**

The Quality and Compliance Manager presented a detailed report on a temperature excursion that occurred on Friday 2 June 2023 in Cold Store 3 (ambient chamber B).

- At approximately 14:20, the continuous temperature monitoring system recorded an alarm for zone 3B. The recorded temperature at alarm point was -18.2°C, exceeding the upper limit of -18.0°C for that zone.
- The alarm was acknowledged by the shift supervisor at 14:25. The supervisor attended the zone and found that the evaporator fan for unit EU-3B-02 had tripped on overload. The fan was reset at 14:40 and the zone temperature returned to -19.1°C by 15:05.
- The maximum temperature recorded during the excursion was -17.4°C at 14:32. The duration above the upper limit was approximately 45 minutes.
- Product affected: 214 pallets of frozen beef and lamb product held for three customers. All affected product was inspected by trained staff. No evidence of thawing or temperature damage was found. The product was deemed fit for purpose and released for dispatch.
- The Quality and Compliance Manager noted that the overload trip was likely caused by ice build-up on the fan blades. This was attributed to the recent high humidity weather and the fact that the defrost cycle for this unit was set to a longer interval than recommended by the manufacturer.
- Corrective actions implemented:
  - The defrost interval for unit EU-3B-02 has been adjusted to match the manufacturer's recommendation.
  - A visual inspection of all evaporator fans in Cold Store 3 was completed on 5 June 2023. No other units showed signs of ice build-up.
  - The maintenance schedule has been updated to include a quarterly inspection of fan blades for ice build-up, with the first inspection to be completed by 30 September 2023.

The committee discussed the report. The Chair asked whether the incident had been reported to the customers whose product was affected. The Warehouse Manager advised that the three customers had been notified by phone on the day of the incident, and that written notifications were sent on 5 June 2023. One customer requested a copy of the temperature data log, which was provided. No other customer concerns were raised.

**Item 16. Sensor Reliability Review**

The Quality and Compliance Manager reported on a review of the temperature sensor network following the 2 June incident.

- The review covered all 42 temperature sensors in the facility, including sensors in cold stores, cool rooms, and the dispatch dock.
- Calibration records were reviewed. All sensors were found to be within their calibration window, with the most recent calibration completed on 28 April 2023.
- The review identified that two sensors in Cold Store 1 (sensors CS1-07 and CS1-08) had recorded readings that were consistently 0.3°C higher than a calibrated handheld probe used for comparison during a routine check on 8 June 2023. These sensors were re-calibrated on 12 June 2023 and are now reading within acceptable tolerance.
- The review also noted that during the 2 June incident, the sensor at zone 3B recorded the temperature correctly, and that the alarm function operated as designed. No issues were identified with the alarm notification system.
- The Quality and Compliance Manager recommended that the sensor network be reviewed annually, with the next review scheduled for June 2024. The committee noted this recommendation.

**Item 17. Recall Protocol Review**

The Quality and Compliance Manager presented an update on the annual review of the product recall protocol.

**Item 18. Incident Log Procedure Update**

The Chair raised a proposal to update the incident log procedure. The Chair noted that the current procedure requires incidents to be logged within 24 hours, but that the recent temperature excursion highlighted the need for a more detailed review of incident log entries, including the requirement to record the time of the initial alarm and the time of the corrective action.

documents.content:
**Item 17. Recall Protocol Review** *(continued)*

The Quality and Compliance Manager tabled the draft of the revised recall protocol, version 3.2, dated 8 June 2023. The key changes from version 3.1 included:

- A requirement to establish a dedicated recall response team within two hours of a confirmed recall decision, with named alternates for each role.
- A revised customer notification template that includes a field for the affected lot code and the temperature excursion duration, where applicable.
- A clarification that the recall decision tree applies to both raw and finished product stored in the facility, including product held on behalf of third-party logistics clients.
- A new section on post-recall review, requiring a written report to be submitted to the committee within 30 days of the conclusion of a recall event.

The committee discussed the resource implications of the two-hour team assembly requirement. The Operations Manager noted that during night shifts, the on-call supervisor would need to be the initial team lead, with the Quality and Compliance Manager joining remotely. This was accepted as a workable interim arrangement.

The Chair asked whether the protocol had been tested against a tabletop exercise. The Quality and Compliance Manager advised that a tabletop exercise was scheduled for 28 June 2023, and that the results would be reported at the July committee meeting.

**Resolution 2023-14: Approval of Revised Recall Protocol**

Moved by the Quality and Compliance Manager, seconded by the Operations Manager:

That the revised product recall protocol, version 3.2, dated 8 June 2023, be approved for implementation effective 1 July 2023, subject to the outcomes of the tabletop exercise scheduled for 28 June 2023.

Motion carried unanimously.

**Item 18. Incident Log Procedure Update** *(continued)*

The Chair noted that the proposal to update the incident log procedure had been circulated in writing prior to the meeting. The proposed changes were:

- To extend the incident log entry requirement from 24 hours to 48 hours, to allow for the collection of complete information where multiple systems are involved.
- To require that the incident log include the time of the initial alarm, the time of the first corrective action, and the time the incident was closed out.
- To require that the person closing out an incident log entry confirm that the temperature data log has been reviewed and attached, where the incident involved a temperature excursion.

The Operations Manager expressed support for the 48-hour window, noting that the current 24-hour requirement had sometimes resulted in incomplete entries being made in haste and then requiring correction. The Quality and Compliance Manager noted that the proposed changes were consistent with the findings of the sensor reliability review.

**Resolution 2023-15: Update to Incident Log Procedure**

Moved by the Chair, seconded by the Quality and Compliance Manager:

That the incident log procedure be updated as circulated, with the revised procedure to take effect on 1 July 2023.

Motion carried.
